bull.b: Two successful pivotal trials materially de-risk the regulatory path for elegrobart and support a planned BLA. Durable impact: regulatory approval potential shifts company from discovery to commercialization, enabling revenue generation, partner interest, and long-term market positioning in thyroid eye disease.

Securing a reputable contract manufacturer establishes scalable commercial supply and reduces execution risk at launch. Long-term, a binding multi-year relationship with flexible sourcing mitigates manufacturing bottlenecks, supports launch planning, and improves go-to-market readiness for potential approved products.

Fresh capital plus termination of the term loan materially improves financial flexibility and reduces future interest obligations. Combined with low leverage, this provides a multi-month runway to fund commercialization and R&D, lowering near-term refinancing risk and supporting strategic investments.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow indicate heavy ongoing funding needs to advance trials and prepare commercialization. This creates persistent reliance on capital markets or partnerships, risks dilution over time, and constrains discretionary investments absent profitable commercialization.

Very large recurring net losses and negative margins reflect scale mismatch between R&D/SG&A spending and current revenue. Long-term profitability requires successful product launches or licensing; until then, returns on equity remain highly negative and investor funding tolerance is a structural risk.

The business model depends on successful regulatory approvals and commercialization to generate sustainable revenue. This creates binary, long-duration execution risk: regulatory setbacks, launch delays, or competitive entries could materially impair projected cash flows and force additional dilutive financings.
